research.notes: FICTIONAL SAMPLE DATA for UI testing. Not a real company.

company.name: Nordvalve Oy (sample)
company.one_liner: Industrial valve manufacturer selling to process industry and utilities across the Nordics.

decision_maker.why_them: Owns order-to-delivery, where most of the manual work in the job ads sits.

why_now.detail: Capacity up ~30%, but the order desk headcount is the same.
Three open roles with near-identical manual tasks suggests the order desk is the bottleneck.

hidden_work.evidence_quote: Kirjaat asiakkaiden sähköpostitilaukset ERP-järjestelmään ja tarkistat hinnat hinnastosta.
hidden_work.evidence_translation: You enter customers' email orders into the ERP and check prices against the price list.
hidden_work.today: Coordinators retype PDF and email orders line by line into the ERP.
hidden_work.fix: An inbox agent that reads incoming orders, pre-fills the ERP order and flags only the exceptions.

hidden_work.evidence_quote: Compile weekly sales and delivery reports in Excel for management.
hidden_work.source_label: Job ad: Sales Analyst, company careers page, Sep 2026
hidden_work.today: Data is exported from ERP and CRM every Monday and stitched together by hand.
hidden_work.fix: A live dashboard fed directly from ERP and CRM, with a Monday summary written automatically.

hidden_work.evidence_quote: Vastaat asiakkaiden toimitusaikatiedusteluihin puhelimitse ja sähköpostitse.
hidden_work.evidence_translation: You answer customers' delivery-time enquiries by phone and email.
hidden_work.today: Each enquiry means looking up the order in the ERP and replying by hand.
hidden_work.fix: Automatic delivery-status replies and a customer status page from ERP data.

first_build.title: An order inbox that types itself
first_build.pitch: Incoming email and PDF orders are read, matched to customers and price lists, and arrive in the ERP as draft orders for a quick human check.
plan: Day 1-2: sample 200 real orders and map the ERP fields
Day 3-7: build the extraction and matching, run it in shadow mode
Day 8-10: coordinators approve drafts instead of typing
Day 11-14: measure time per order and hand over
first_build.impact: Target: order entry time down by 60–70% within a month.
first_build.time_back_to: Coordinators move from retyping to following up open quotes and key accounts while Kangasala ramps up.
first_build.data_needed: Read access to the order inbox, the price list, and the ERP order import. No changes to the ERP itself.

risks.risk: A wrong order reaches a customer
risks.safeguard: Every draft is approved by a coordinator before it is sent to the ERP. Shadow mode first, on 200 real orders.
Runs in your own cloud tenant, EU region only, under your existing GDPR processes.

risks.risk: We become dependent on a vendor
risks.safeguard: You own the code and the prompts. Your IT team gets a handover in week 2.

microsite.headline: Your job ads describe about 30 hours a week of retyping.
microsite.subhead: We read what Nordvalve has published about its own work. Here's what we found, and what we'd fix first.
microsite.opener: You're hiring three coordinators while a new line adds 30% capacity. Most of what those roles describe is moving data from emails into the ERP, and that's exactly the kind of work we remove.
microsite.closing: Worth 20 minutes before you make those three hires?

objections.objection: Our ERP vendor can do this.
objections.answer: Maybe, on their roadmap. We ship in two weeks on top of what you have, and it works with any ERP that accepts imports.
That's why we start in shadow mode on 200 real orders and show you the hit rate before anyone relies on it.

objections.objection: We don't have time for an IT project.
objections.answer: It's two weeks and about three hours of your team's time. The point is to give time back.

priorities: On-time delivery as the new line ramps up
persona.style: Engineer by background, direct, short sentences, wants numbers.
